areas.title: Data types
areas.intro: Polars has a closed set of Arrow-backed data types. Nanuq has a DataType for each, built from Nim types (dataType(T)) and printed as Nanuq code.
areas.differences: A plain DataType value with kind and parameters instead of Python's class hierarchy; nulls are Option[T].

areas.title: Series
areas.intro: Since 0.4 a Series is a full column: built from Nim, taken out of a frame, and computed with through expressions.
areas.differences: Series methods run as expressions on a one-column frame instead of binding the Rust Series API twice. Aggregations return a one-value Series; read the scalar with item.

rows.note: Every scalar, temporal and nested type, with Option[T] for nulls.

areas.title: DataFrame (eager)
areas.intro: The eager API. Most verbs run through the lazy engine, as in Polars itself.
areas.differences: Python DataFrames are mutable (df['a'] = s); Nanuq frames are immutable refs and every edit returns a new frame, like the Rust API.

areas.title: Expressions: core

areas.differences: Nim operators cover arithmetic and comparison; and/or/not replace & | ~. Polars' method spellings (add, mul, eq, ...) also exist since 0.6. Python's method parameter is how in Nanuq.
